hints: Normal gradient is $-\frac{1}{3} \implies$ tangent gradient is $3$.
Point on normal is $(4, 7)$, substitute into curve to find $k = 11$.
walkthrough:
Find the gradient of the normal line $3y + x = 25 \implies y = -\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{25}{3}$:
$$m_N = -\frac{1}{3} \implies m_T = -\frac{1}{-1/3} = 3$$

Differentiate the curve equation $y = x^2 - 5x + k$ and equate to the tangent gradient:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x - 5 = 3 \implies 2x = 8 \implies x = 4$$

Find the $y$-coordinate of the contact point on the normal line at $x = 4$:
$$3y + 4 = 25 \implies 3y = 21 \implies y = 7 \implies (4, 7)$$

Substitute $(4, 7)$ into the curve equation to determine $k$:
$$7 = 4^2 - 5(4) + k = 16 - 20 + k = -4 + k \implies k = 11$$

ai_rubric.Normal and Tangent Condition: Finds tangent gradient $3$ (B2). Solves $2x - 5 = 3 \implies x = 4$ (M1, A1). Substitutes $(4, 7)$ to find $k = 11$ (DM1, A1).
